issue.title: Cut per-link wire conversion cost (~24us/link) in the sase-core document-link scan

task_type_fields.proposal: Proposed by sase-1es.8 (note #5) and named in plan:202610/pager_performance.md (root cause 2): the Rust document-link scan behind `sase.artifact_ref_operations.scan_artifact_ref_document` costs about 24 us per link in wire conversion (Rust -> Python ArtifactRefDocumentTarget objects), so 100k links cost about 2.4s per scan. Epic sase-1es memoized the scan per section object (`section_target_spans`) and made the Python side near-linear (`scan_links` 20k link-dense 21s -> 0.45s). The remaining per-link cost is in the binding. It dominates link-dense opens (100k log-dense pager mount 20.5s). Proposal: in the linked sase-core repo, cut the per-link conversion cost of the document-link scan wire. Options include a columnar/struct-of-arrays result, lazily materialized target objects, or skipping fields the pager does not read. Then update the Python adapter in src/sase/artifact_ref_operations.py. Measure with `just bench-pager --cases log-dense --ladder 20000,100000 --no-cold`.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-1es's guardrails kept the Rust link grammar unchanged and only changed Python glue. This work belongs in the sase-core crate (Rust core backend boundary), needs a sase-core-revision pin bump, and was explicitly out of the epic's scope.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1es made the Python side of pager link scanning near-linear, leaving the Rust binding's per-link conversion as the dominant cost of link-dense opens; the epic plan assigns it to sase-core.

payload.description: Rust per-link conversion dominates link-dense (log-dense) opens; sase-1fb covers the rest of the open cost
